prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The provision for credit losses decreased by $22 million from the quarter ended September 30, 2025. This decrease included a $26 million decrease in the provision for credit losses - loans, as well as a $4 million increase in the provision for credit losses - unfunded commitments. The current year provision was driven by growth in our commercial lending portfolio. The prior year provision for credit losses - loans was driven by the initial Day 1 provision from the Penns Woods acquisition of $20.6 million. Excluding the Day 1 provision for credit losses from the acquisition, the provision for credit losses for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 was $10.5 million, which was driven by an increase in net charge offs coupled with an increase due to individually assessed loans. This increase in provision for unfunded was due to growth in our undrawn commitments.

Additionally, the Company saw an increase in classified loans of $16 million to $469 million, or 3.50% of total loans, at September 30, 2026 compared to $453 million , or 3.49% of total loans, at December 31, 2025. This increase was driven by an increase in classified loans within our commercial real estate portfolio which increased $15 million driven by acquired loans to borrowers whose updated financial statements indicated financial deterioration.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The provision for income taxes increased by $16 million from the quarter ended September 30, 2025 and $25 million from the nine months ended September 30, 2025. These increases were driven by higher income before taxes, primarily resulting from increased interest income associated with the acquisition, which expanded our loan portfolio.

The provision for income taxes is primarily driven by changes in our current period income before taxes. We anticipate our effective tax rate to be between 23.0% and 25.0% for the year ending December 31, 2026.

Net interest income.text: To make it easier to compare both the results across several periods and the yields on various types of earning assets (some taxable, some not), we present net interest income in the discussion below on a fully taxable equivalent “FTE basis” (i.e., as if all income were taxable and at the same rate). For example, $100 of tax-exempt income would be presented as $126, an amount that, if taxed at the statutory federal income tax rate of 21%, would yield $100. See the "GAAP to Non-GAAP Reconciliations" for information regarding tax-equivalent adjustments and GAAP results.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
(a) Other noninterest income includes gain on sale of investments, gain on real estate owned, net, mortgage banking income, and other operating income. See the "Consolidated Statements of Income" in Item 1. Financial Statements of this report.

Noninterest income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was $36 million, an increase of $4 million from the quarter ended September 30, 2025, driven by an increase $1 million in service charges and fees driven by deposit related fees based on customer activity related to the Penns Woods acquisition and a $2 million increase in trust and other financial services income driven by an increase in our wealth management business.

Noninterest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $103 million, an increase of $11 million from the nine months ended September 30, 2025, driven by an increase of $4 million in service charges and fees and a $4 million increase in trust and other financial services income driven by the same factors discussed above.

intro.text: Northwest Bancshares, Inc., a Maryland corporation, was incorporated in 2009 to be the successor corporation to Northwest Bancorp, Inc., the former stock holding company for Northwest Bank, upon completion of the mutual-to-stock conversion of Northwest Bancorp, MHC. The terms “Northwest”, “the Company”, “we”, “us” and “our” refer to Northwest Bancshares, Inc., unless indicated otherwise by the context. The conversion was completed in 2009 when the Company sold 68,878,267 shares of common stock at $10.00 per share in the related offering. Concurrent with the completion of the offering, shares of Northwest Bancorp, Inc. common stock owned by public stockholders were exchanged for shares of Northwest Bancshares, Inc.’s common stock.
